Analysis and results for the manuscript Results section.

-   Reads `data/processed/participants.csv` (written by [`R/clean.R`](../R/clean.R)); everything else is computed here.
-   See [README.qmd](README.qmd) for data quality and exclusions.
-   Companion to [results.qmd](results.qmd). Identical data preparation, descriptive statistics and association models; three inference steps are re-fitted with posterior sampling. Each is marked "Bayesian" in the text below, and the frequentist fit is retained alongside it as a comparison.

The three:

| Step | Frequentist version | Why it is re-fitted |
|------------------------|------------------------|------------------------|
| BMI slope during follow-up | `lmer` + profile CI | The claim is that BMI recovered. A posterior gives `P(slope > 0)` and `P(slope > clinically meaningful)` directly, and puts an interval on the variance components that `lmer` reports as bare point estimates. |
| Slope by age group | Wald intervals, no p-values | The frequentist caption has to say "an interval spanning zero is not evidence of no difference". A posterior states the probability instead. |
| Selection checks | t-tests read as "no difference" | These argue for equivalence. A non-significant t-test cannot support that; an equivalence test against a region of practical equivalence can. |

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| cache: false

set.seed(20260612)

pacman::p_load(
  here,
  readr,
  dplyr,
  tidyr,
  purrr,
  stringr,
  forcats,
  lubridate,
  broom,
  broom.helpers,
  broom.mixed,
  lme4,
  performance,
  binom,
  mgcv,
  rstanarm,
  bayestestR,
  knitr,
  ggplot2,
  scales
)

# rstanarm models are precompiled, so no Stan toolchain compile step is needed.
options(mc.cores = max(1, parallel::detectCores() - 1))

# Sampler settings, applied to every fit below
n_chains <- 4
n_iter <- 4000
stan_seed <- 20260612

knitr::opts_chunk$set(autodep = TRUE)

theme_set(theme_bw() + theme(legend.position = "bottom"))

# Factor level orders. The first level of each is the regression reference.
age_levels <- c("Age under 30", "Age 30-45", "Age over 45")
sex_levels <- c("Female", "Male")
governorate_levels <- c(
  "Deir Al Balah",
  "Gaza City, North Gaza",
  "Khan Yunis, Rafah"
)
role_levels <- c("National staff", "Casual worker", "Other")
chronic_levels <- c("No chronic condition", "Chronic condition")
children_levels <- c("0", "1", "2", "3+")
cohort_levels <- c("Aug-Sep 2025", "Oct-Nov 2025")
bmi_levels <- c("Underweight", "Normal", "Overweight", "Obese")

# Display labels, used for both model output and comparison tables
variable_labels <- c(
  age = "Age group",
  sex = "Sex",
  governorate_cat = "Governorate of residence",
  children = "Dependent children < 10y",
  role_cat = "Professional role",
  entry_cohort = "Month of study entry",
  chronic = "Chronic condition",
  bmi_prewar = "Pre-war BMI (per kg/m2)",
  bmi_entry = "BMI at study entry (kg/m2)",
  pct_weight_change = "Weight change since pre-war (%)",
  age_years = "Age (years)"
)

days_per_month <- 30

fmt_ci <- function(estimate, low, high, digits = 1) {
  sprintf(
    paste0("%.", digits, "f (%.", digits, "f to %.", digits, "f)"),
    estimate,
    low,
    high
  )
}

fmt_pct <- function(x, digits = 1) {
  sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f%%"), x)
}

fmt_p <- function(p) {
  format.pval(p, digits = 2, eps = 0.001)
}

# Posterior probabilities are never rounded to 0 or 1: with 8000 draws the
# resolution is 1/8000, so report the bound rather than implying certainty.
fmt_prob <- function(p) {
  case_when(
    p > 0.9995 ~ "> 0.999",
    p < 0.0005 ~ "< 0.001",
    .default = sprintf("%.3f", p)
  )
}

# Draws for one model term, rescaled from per-day to per-30-day
slope_draws <- function(fit, term) {
  as.numeric(as.matrix(fit, pars = term)) * days_per_month
}

# Posterior median, 95% credible interval, and the probability of exceeding
# each of a named set of thresholds
summarise_draws <- function(draws, thresholds = c(`P(> 0)` = 0)) {
  quantiles <- quantile(draws, c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975))
  probabilities <- map(thresholds, \(threshold) mean(draws > threshold))

  tibble(
    median = quantiles[[2]],
    conf.low = quantiles[[1]],
    conf.high = quantiles[[3]],
    !!!probabilities
  )
}
```

Participants entered in two waves, August-September and October-November 2025, because the study was re-advertised in October.
That risks confounding any comparison over calendar time with the changing composition of the sample.
Descriptive statistics are therefore reported separately by entry wave, `entry_cohort` is a covariate in the longitudinal models, and the two waves are compared directly in the selection checks at the end.

```{r}
#| label: participant-sets
#| cache.extra: !expr file.mtime(here::here("data", "processed", "participants.csv"))

data_processed <- read_csv(
  here("data", "processed", "participants.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

included <- data_processed |>
  filter(record_remove == "include", !is.na(weight)) |>
  mutate(
    record_date = as_date(record_date),
    date_entry = as_date(date_entry),
    entry_cohort = if_else(
      date_entry < as_date("2025-10-01"),
      "Aug-Sep 2025",
      "Oct-Nov 2025"
    ),
    # North Gaza (n = 20) and Rafah (n = 8) are too sparse to estimate separately
    governorate_cat = case_when(
      governorate %in% c("Gaza City", "North Gaza") ~ "Gaza City, North Gaza",
      governorate %in% c("Khan Yunis", "Rafah") ~ "Khan Yunis, Rafah",
      governorate == "Deir Al Balah" ~ "Deir Al Balah"
    ),
    # collapse sparse employment categories
    role_cat = case_when(
      role == "National staff" ~ "National staff",
      role == "Casual/daily worker" ~ "Casual worker",
      is.na(role) ~ NA_character_,
      TRUE ~ "Other"
    ),
    # ODK multi-select: "0" = no condition reported, any code = at least one
    chronic = case_when(
      is.na(chronic_condition) ~ NA_character_,
      chronic_condition == "0" ~ "No chronic condition",
      TRUE ~ "Chronic condition"
    )
  ) |>
  mutate(
    age = factor(age, levels = age_levels),
    sex = factor(sex, levels = sex_levels),
    governorate_cat = factor(governorate_cat, levels = governorate_levels),
    role_cat = factor(role_cat, levels = role_levels),
    chronic = factor(chronic, levels = chronic_levels),
    children = factor(children, levels = children_levels),
    entry_cohort = factor(entry_cohort, levels = cohort_levels)
  ) |>
  add_count(id, name = "n_obs")

# Cross-sectional set: one row per participant at entry.
# Outcome is change from pre-war to the first measured weight.
baseline <- included |>
  filter(record_number == 1) |>
  mutate(
    pct_weight_change = 100 * (weight_entry - weight_prewar) / weight_prewar,
    bmi_change = bmi_entry - bmi_prewar,
    lost_5pct = pct_weight_change <= -5,
    lost_10pct = pct_weight_change <= -10,
    underweight_prewar = bmi_prewar < 18.5,
    underweight_entry = bmi_entry < 18.5,
    bmi_under20_entry = bmi_entry < 20,
    has_followup = n_obs >= 2
  )

cross_sectional <- filter(baseline, !is.na(weight_prewar))

# Longitudinal set: participants with 2+ included records. Two participants are
# dropped for an implausible between-visit rate of BMI change (>= 1 kg/m2/day),
# matching the exclusion applied in R/visualise.R.
longitudinal_all <- included |>
  filter(n_obs >= 2) |>
  arrange(id, record_date) |>
  group_by(id) |>
  mutate(
    bmi_daily_change = c(NA, diff(bmi)) / c(NA, as.numeric(diff(record_date)))
  ) |>
  ungroup()

implausible_ids <- longitudinal_all |>
  filter(abs(bmi_daily_change) >= 1) |>
  pull(id) |>
  unique()

longitudinal <- longitudinal_all |>
  filter(!id %in% implausible_ids) |>
  mutate(id = factor(id))
```

-   `r nrow(baseline)` participants were measured at study entry, of whom `r nrow(cross_sectional)` recalled a pre-war weight.
-   `r n_distinct(longitudinal_all$id)` returned for at least one further measurement
    -   `r n_distinct(longitudinal$id)` of those are analysed, after `r length(implausible_ids)` were dropped for an implausible rate of BMI change (\>= 1 kg/m2/day).

## Change from pre-war to study entry

```{r}
#| label: descriptive-change

summarise_change <- function(data) {
  data |>
    summarise(
      n = n(),
      across(
        c(pct_weight_change, bmi_change),
        list(
          mean = ~ mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
          sd = ~ sd(.x, na.rm = TRUE)
        )
      ),
      across(
        pct_weight_change,
        list(
          median = ~ median(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
          p25 = ~ quantile(.x, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
          p75 = ~ quantile(.x, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE)
        )
      ),
      pct_lost_5pct = 100 * mean(lost_5pct, na.rm = TRUE),
      pct_lost_10pct = 100 * mean(lost_10pct, na.rm = TRUE),
      pct_underweight_entry = 100 * mean(underweight_entry, na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
}

descriptive <- bind_rows(
  cross_sectional |>
    summarise_change() |>
    mutate(group = "Overall", .before = 1),
  cross_sectional |>
    group_by(group = as.character(entry_cohort)) |>
    summarise_change()
)

# Mean change with a 95% CI
headline <- bind_rows(
  tidy(t.test(cross_sectional$pct_weight_change)) |>
    mutate(outcome = "Weight change since pre-war (%)"),
  tidy(t.test(cross_sectional$bmi_change)) |>
    mutate(outcome = "BMI change since pre-war (kg/m2)")
) |>
  transmute(
    outcome,
    n = nrow(cross_sectional),
    mean = estimate,
    conf.low,
    conf.high
  )

# Prevalence of each malnutrition-adjacent threshold (per NICE), Wilson 95% CIs
prevalence_ci <- function(indicator, label, timeframe) {
  indicator <- indicator[!is.na(indicator)]
  binom.confint(sum(indicator), length(indicator), methods = "wilson") |>
    transmute(
      indicator = label,
      timeframe = timeframe,
      n_positive = x, # binom.confint's successes column
      n = n,
      pct = 100 * mean,
      pct_low = 100 * lower,
      pct_high = 100 * upper
    )
}

thresholds <- bind_rows(
  prevalence_ci(
    cross_sectional$underweight_prewar,
    "BMI < 18.5 kg/m2",
    "Pre-war (recalled, Oct 2023)"
  ),
  prevalence_ci(
    cross_sectional$underweight_entry,
    "BMI < 18.5 kg/m2",
    "At study entry (measured)"
  ),
  prevalence_ci(
    cross_sectional$bmi_under20_entry,
    "BMI < 20 kg/m2",
    "At study entry (measured)"
  ),
  prevalence_ci(
    cross_sectional$lost_5pct,
    "Lost >= 5% of body weight",
    "Pre-war to study entry (~22 months)"
  ),
  prevalence_ci(
    cross_sectional$lost_10pct,
    "Lost >= 10% of body weight",
    "Pre-war to study entry (~22 months)"
  )
)
```

Among `r nrow(cross_sectional)` participants who recalled a pre-war weight:

```{r}
#| label: tbl-headline
#| tbl-cap: "Mean change from self-recalled pre-war (October 2023) to first measured weight at study entry."

headline |>
  transmute(
    Outcome = outcome,
    N = n,
    `Mean change (95% CI)` = fmt_ci(mean, conf.low, conf.high, 2)
  ) |>
  kable()
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-thresholds
#| tbl-cap: >-
#|   Prevalence of low BMI and of substantial weight loss, with Wilson 95% confidence intervals.
#|   Components are reported separately with their own reference periods rather than combined into a composite malnutrition definition (see note below).

thresholds |>
  transmute(
    Indicator = indicator,
    `Reference period` = timeframe,
    `n / N` = paste0(n_positive, " / ", n),
    `% (95% CI)` = fmt_ci(pct, pct_low, pct_high)
  ) |>
  kable()
```

Note on composite definitions: the NICE malnutrition criteria require unintentional weight loss over a 3 to 6 month window.
The pre-war reference here is roughly 22 months earlier, so the composite does not apply to this comparison, and within the study window the trend is recovery rather than loss.
The components are therefore reported separately, each with its reference period stated.

```{r}
descriptive |>
```

## Associations with change since pre-war

Linear regression of change since pre-war on each participant characteristic, in three specifications.
`Univariable` fits one exposure at a time.
`Adjusted` fits all characteristics simultaneously.
`Adjusted + pre-war BMI` adds pre-war BMI, which tests whether apparent differences simply reflect how heavy participants were to begin with: a participant who started heavier has more weight available to lose.

Chronic condition is held out of the adjusted models because it was only asked after August 2025 and is missing for two thirds of participants.
It is reported univariably, plus one adjusted model restricted to those who were asked.

```{r}
#| label: associations

exposures <- c(
  "age",
  "sex",
  "governorate_cat",
  "children",
  "role_cat",
  "entry_cohort"
)

outcomes <- c(
  pct_weight_change = "Weight change since pre-war (%)",
  bmi_change = "BMI change since pre-war (kg/m2)"
)

fit_assoc <- function(data,
                      outcome_var,
                      predictors,
                      model_label,
                      keep_variables = predictors) {
  model_formula <- reformulate(predictors, response = outcome_var)
  fit <- lm(model_formula, data = data)
  tidy_plus_plus(
    fit,
    conf.int = TRUE,
    variable_labels = variable_labels,
    add_header_rows = FALSE,
    add_reference_rows = FALSE
  ) |>
    filter(variable %in% keep_variables) |>
    transmute(
      model = model_label,
      variable,
      variable_label = var_label,
      # factor terms carry their contrast level; continuous terms are per-unit
      level = if_else(is.na(contrasts), "per unit", label),
      estimate,
      conf.low,
      conf.high,
      p.value,
      n_model = stats::nobs(fit)
    )
}

fit_all_specifications <- function(data, outcome_var) {
  bind_rows(
    # 1. univariable, one model per exposure
    map(
      c(exposures, "chronic", "bmi_prewar"),
      \(exposure) fit_assoc(data, outcome_var, exposure, "Univariable")
    ) |>
      list_rbind(),
    # 2. mutually adjusted
    fit_assoc(data, outcome_var, exposures, "Adjusted"),
    # 3. mutually adjusted, plus pre-war BMI
    fit_assoc(
      data,
      outcome_var,
      c(exposures, "bmi_prewar"),
      "Adjusted + pre-war BMI"
    )
  ) |>
    mutate(outcome = unname(outcomes[outcome_var]), .before = 1)
}

associations <- names(outcomes) |>
  map(\(outcome_var) fit_all_specifications(cross_sectional, outcome_var)) |>
  list_rbind() |>
  mutate(
    model = factor(
      model,
      levels = c("Univariable", "Adjusted", "Adjusted + pre-war BMI")
    )
  ) |>
  arrange(outcome, model, variable, level)

# Chronic condition, adjusted, restricted to participants who were asked
chronic_adjusted <- names(outcomes) |>
  map(\(outcome_var) {
    fit_assoc(
      filter(cross_sectional, !is.na(chronic)),
      outcome_var,
      c(exposures, "chronic"),
      "Adjusted (restricted to those asked)",
      keep_variables = "chronic"
    ) |>
      mutate(outcome = unname(outcomes[outcome_var]), .before = 1)
  }) |>
  list_rbind()

table_associations <- function(outcome_name) {
  associations |>
    filter(outcome == outcome_name) |>
    mutate(
      cell = paste0(
        fmt_ci(estimate, conf.low, conf.high, 2),
        " p=",
        fmt_p(p.value)
      )
    ) |>
    select(Characteristic = variable_label, Level = level, model, cell) |>
    pivot_wider(
      names_from = model,
      values_from = cell,
      values_fill = "not in model"
    ) |>
    kable()
}

plot_forest <- function(outcome_name, x_label) {
  associations |>
    filter(
      outcome == outcome_name,
      model != "Univariable",
      variable != "bmi_prewar"
    ) |>
    mutate(
      label = paste0(variable_label, ": ", level),
      label = fct_rev(fct_inorder(label))
    ) |>
    ggplot(aes(x = estimate, y = label, colour = model)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = 2, colour = "grey40") +
    geom_pointrange(
      aes(xmin = conf.low, xmax = conf.high),
      position = position_dodge(width = 0.5),
      size = 0.3
    ) +
    scale_colour_manual(
      values = c(
        "Adjusted" = "#01454f",
        "Adjusted + pre-war BMI" = "#ffa600"
      ),
      name = NULL
    ) +
    labs(x = x_label, y = NULL)
}
```

Estimates are percentage points, relative to the reference level.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-associations-weight
#| tbl-cap: >-
#|   Difference in percent weight change since pre-war, by participant characteristic.
#|   Reference levels: age 30-45, female, Deir Al Balah, no dependent children, national staff, entry Aug-Sep 2025.
#|   North Gaza (n=20) is combined with Gaza City and Rafah (n=8) with Khan Yunis because both are too sparse to estimate separately.

table_associations("Weight change since pre-war (%)")
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-associations-bmi
#| tbl-cap: >-
#|   Difference in absolute BMI change since pre-war (kg/m2), by participant characteristic.
#|   Same models and reference levels as the table above.

table_associations("BMI change since pre-war (kg/m2)")
```

Chronic condition, fitted on the subset who were asked:

```{r}

chronic_adjusted |>

  ) |>

```

```{r}
#| label: fig-forest-weight
#| fig-cap: >-
#|   Difference in percent weight change since pre-war by participant characteristic, mutually adjusted and additionally adjusted for pre-war BMI.
#|   Points are estimates, bars are 95% confidence intervals.
#|   Negative values indicate greater weight loss than the reference level.

#| fig-height: 7
```

## BMI categories, pre-war to study entry

```{r}
#| label: bmi-categories

# One long table of WHO category by period, feeding both the counts and the pyramid
bmi_category_long <- cross_sectional |>
  select(
    id,
    entry_cohort,
    sex,
    age,
    `Pre-war` = bmi_category_prewar,
    `Study entry` = bmi_category_entry
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(
    c(`Pre-war`, `Study entry`),
    names_to = "period",
    values_to = "bmi_category"
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(bmi_category)) |>
  mutate(
    period = factor(period, levels = c("Pre-war", "Study entry")),
    bmi_category = factor(bmi_category, levels = bmi_levels)
  )

bmi_categories <- bmi_category_long |>
  count(entry_cohort, period, bmi_category) |>
  group_by(entry_cohort, period) |>
  mutate(pct = 100 * n / sum(n)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  arrange(entry_cohort, period, bmi_category)

# Transition matrix: where each pre-war category ended up at study entry
bmi_transitions <- cross_sectional |>
  filter(!is.na(bmi_category_prewar), !is.na(bmi_category_entry)) |>
  count(bmi_category_prewar, bmi_category_entry) |>
  group_by(bmi_category_prewar) |>
  mutate(pct_of_prewar_category = 100 * n / sum(n)) |>
  ungroup()

# Overweight or obese pre-war, normal or underweight at entry
category_shift <- cross_sectional |>
  filter(!is.na(bmi_category_prewar), !is.na(bmi_category_entry)) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    pct_overweight_obese_prewar = 100 *
      mean(bmi_category_prewar %in% c("Overweight", "Obese")),
    pct_overweight_obese_entry = 100 *
      mean(bmi_category_entry %in% c("Overweight", "Obese")),
    pct_moved_down = 100 *
      mean(
        bmi_category_prewar %in% c("Overweight", "Obese") &
          bmi_category_entry %in% c("Normal", "Underweight")
      )
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-category-shift
#| tbl-cap: "Movement between WHO BMI categories from pre-war to study entry."

category_shift |>
  transmute(
    N = n,
    `Overweight or obese pre-war` = fmt_pct(pct_overweight_obese_prewar),
    `Overweight or obese at entry` = fmt_pct(pct_overweight_obese_entry),
    `Moved from overweight/obese to normal/underweight` = fmt_pct(pct_moved_down)
  ) |>
  kable()
```

This shift is depletion from a high starting point, not an improvement in health.
Read it alongside the mean BMI drop of `r sprintf("%.1f kg/m2", headline$mean[headline$outcome == "BMI change since pre-war (kg/m2)"])` and the rise in underweight prevalence from `r fmt_pct(thresholds$pct[thresholds$timeframe == "Pre-war (recalled, Oct 2023)"])` to `r fmt_pct(thresholds$pct[thresholds$indicator == "BMI < 18.5 kg/m2" & thresholds$timeframe == "At study entry (measured)"])`.

```{r}
#| label: fig-bmi-categories
#| fig-cap: >-
#|   Distribution of WHO BMI categories pre-war and at study entry, by entry cohort.
#|   Percentages within each cohort and time point.

bmi_categories |>
  ggplot(aes(x = period, y = pct, fill = bmi_category)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~entry_cohort) +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(direction = -1, name = "BMI category") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_percent(scale = 1)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Participants")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-age-sex-pyramid
#| fig-cap: "Age-sex distribution by BMI category, pre-war and at study entry."

bmi_category_long |>
  filter(!is.na(sex), !is.na(age)) |>
  count(period, sex, age, bmi_category) |>
  mutate(n_signed = if_else(sex == "Male", -n, n)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = n_signed, y = age, fill = bmi_category)) +
  geom_col() +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "#01454f", linewidth = 0.3) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = abs) +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(direction = -1, name = "BMI category") +
  facet_wrap(~period) +
  labs(x = "Participants  (Male <- | -> Female)", y = NULL)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-transitions
#| tbl-cap: >-
#|   Where each pre-war BMI category ended up at study entry.
#|   Row percentages.

bmi_transitions |>
  mutate(cell = sprintf("%d (%.0f%%)", n, pct_of_prewar_category)) |>
  select(bmi_category_prewar, bmi_category_entry, cell) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = bmi_category_entry,
    values_from = cell,
    values_fill = "-"
  ) |>
  rename(`Pre-war category` = bmi_category_prewar) |>
  kable()
```

## BMI trend during follow-up

Among `r n_distinct(longitudinal$id)` participants with two or more measurements (`r nrow(longitudinal)` observations).
Two participants were excluded for an implausible between-visit rate of BMI change (\>= 1 kg/m2 per day).

The model is a linear mixed model, `BMI ~ days since entry + entry cohort + (1 | id)`.
Time is measured from each participant's own entry, so the slope is within-person change.
Entry cohort absorbs the difference in starting point between early and late joiners.

Fitted twice: by maximum likelihood with `lme4`, and by posterior sampling with `rstanarm`.
Priors are the rstanarm defaults, which are weakly informative and rescaled to the data: a `normal(0, 2.5)` prior on each coefficient and on the intercept, scaled by the standard deviations of outcome and predictor, and an `exponential(1)` prior on the residual standard deviation, scaled by the standard deviation of the outcome.
On `r nrow(longitudinal)` observations these priors are dominated by the likelihood; they exist to regularise, not to contribute information.

```{r}
#| label: longitudinal-models

lmm_bmi_time <- lmer(
  bmi ~ days_since_entry + entry_cohort + (1 | id),
  data = longitudinal
)

slope_ci <- confint(
  lmm_bmi_time,
  method = "profile",
  parm = "days_since_entry"
)

# Rescale the daily slope to BMI change per 30 days
lmm_slope <- tidy(lmm_bmi_time, effects = "fixed") |>
  filter(term == "days_since_entry") |>
  transmute(
    estimate_per_30d = estimate * days_per_month,
    conf.low_per_30d = slope_ci[1] * days_per_month,
    conf.high_per_30d = slope_ci[2] * days_per_month
  )

lmm_r2 <- r2(lmm_bmi_time)

# Effect modification by age group: the draft claims under-30s regained faster
lmm_bmi_time_age <- lmer(
  bmi ~ days_since_entry * age + entry_cohort + (1 | id),
  data = longitudinal
)

lmm_age <- tidy(lmm_bmi_time_age, effects = "fixed", conf.int = TRUE) |>
  filter(str_detect(term, "days_since_entry")) |>
  transmute(
    term,
    estimate_per_30d = estimate * days_per_month,
    conf.low_per_30d = conf.low * days_per_month,
    conf.high_per_30d = conf.high * days_per_month,
    statistic
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: bayes-longitudinal-models

bayes_bmi_time <- stan_lmer(
  bmi ~ days_since_entry + entry_cohort + (1 | id),
  data = longitudinal,
  chains = n_chains,
  iter = n_iter,
  seed = stan_seed,
  refresh = 0
)

bayes_bmi_time_age <- stan_lmer(
  bmi ~ days_since_entry * age + entry_cohort + (1 | id),
  data = longitudinal,
  chains = n_chains,
  iter = n_iter,
  seed = stan_seed,
  refresh = 0
)

# Convergence: R-hat should be at or below 1.01 and bulk ESS in the thousands
sampler_diagnostics <- map(
  list(
    `BMI ~ time + cohort` = bayes_bmi_time,
    `BMI ~ time * age + cohort` = bayes_bmi_time_age
  ),
  \(fit) {
    summary_matrix <- summary(fit)
    tibble(
      max_rhat = max(summary_matrix[, "Rhat"], na.rm = TRUE),
      min_ess = min(summary_matrix[, "n_eff"], na.rm = TRUE),
      divergences = sum(rstan::get_divergent_iterations(fit$stanfit))
    )
  }
) |>
  list_rbind(names_to = "model")

# A clinically meaningful rate of recovery, taken from the same NICE threshold
# used for loss: regaining 5% of body weight over six months. Converted to a
# BMI change per 30 days at this sample's median height and entry weight, so the
# threshold comes from the data rather than being asserted.
median_height <- median(longitudinal$height, na.rm = TRUE)
median_weight_entry <- median(longitudinal$weight_entry, na.rm = TRUE)
meaningful_gain_30d <- (0.05 * median_weight_entry / 6) / median_height^2

slope_thresholds <- c(`P(recovery)` = 0, `P(meaningful)` = meaningful_gain_30d)

bayes_slope <- slope_draws(bayes_bmi_time, "days_since_entry") |>
  summarise_draws(slope_thresholds)

# Variance components, which lme4 reports without any measure of uncertainty
bayes_variance <- as.matrix(
  bayes_bmi_time,
  regex_pars = c("^Sigma\\[id", "^sigma$")
) |>
  as_tibble() |>
  rename(var_id = 1, sigma = 2) |>
  transmute(sd_random_intercept = sqrt(var_id), sd_residual = sigma) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "component", values_to = "draw") |>
  group_by(component) |>
  summarise(
    median = median(draw),
    conf.low = quantile(draw, 0.025),
    conf.high = quantile(draw, 0.975),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-sampler
#| tbl-cap: >-
#|   Sampler diagnostics for the two mixed models.
#|   R-hat at or below 1.01 with no divergent transitions indicates the chains converged and the posterior is being explored properly.

sampler_diagnostics |>
  transmute(
    Model = model,
    `Max R-hat` = sprintf("%.3f", max_rhat),
    `Min effective sample size` = round(min_ess),
    `Divergent transitions` = divergences
  ) |>
  kable()
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-lmm
#| tbl-cap: >-
#|   Within-person BMI change during follow-up, per 30 days, from both fits.
#|   The maximum likelihood row carries a 95% confidence interval; the Bayesian row a 95% credible interval.

bind_rows(
  lmm_slope |>
    transmute(
      Fit = "Maximum likelihood (lme4)",
      `Estimate (95% interval)` = fmt_ci(
        estimate_per_30d,
        conf.low_per_30d,
        conf.high_per_30d,
        3
      )
    ),
  bayes_slope |>
    transmute(
      Fit = "Posterior (rstanarm)",
      `Estimate (95% interval)` = fmt_ci(median, conf.low, conf.high, 3)
    )
) |>
  kable()
```

The posterior answers the question the paper actually asks.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-lmm-probabilities
#| tbl-cap: >-
#|   Posterior probabilities for the within-person BMI slope.
#|   The meaningful threshold is the rate that would regain 5% of body weight over six months, the mirror of the NICE loss criterion, evaluated at this sample's median height and entry weight.

bayes_slope |>
  transmute(
    `Median gain per 30 days (95% CrI)` = fmt_ci(median, conf.low, conf.high, 3),
    `P(BMI rising)` = fmt_prob(`P(recovery)`),
    `Meaningful rate (kg/m2 per 30 days)` = sprintf(
      "%.3f",
      meaningful_gain_30d
    ),
    `P(gain exceeds meaningful rate)` = fmt_prob(`P(meaningful)`)
  ) |>
  kable()
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-slope-posterior
#| fig-cap: >-
#|   Posterior for the within-person BMI slope, per 30 days.
#|   The dashed line is no change; the solid line is the clinically meaningful rate of recovery.
#| fig-height: 3
#| fig-width: 7

tibble(draw = slope_draws(bayes_bmi_time, "days_since_entry")) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = draw)) +
  geom_density(fill = "#01454f", colour = NA, alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = 2, colour = "grey30") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = meaningful_gain_30d, colour = "#ffa600") +
  labs(x = "BMI change per 30 days (kg/m2)", y = NULL)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-lmm-fit
#| tbl-cap: >-
#|   Variance components, with 95% credible intervals from the posterior.
#|   The random intercept SD is much larger than the residual SD because BMI varies far more between participants than within them over four months; marginal R2 is correspondingly small.
#|   lme4 reports these two standard deviations as point estimates with no uncertainty attached, which is the practical gain here.

bind_rows(
  bayes_variance |>
    mutate(
      Component = if_else(
        component == "sd_random_intercept",
        "SD between participants",
        "SD within participants (residual)"
      ),
      `Posterior median (95% CrI)` = fmt_ci(median, conf.low, conf.high, 2),
      .keep = "none"
    )
) |>
  kable()
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-lmm-r2
#| tbl-cap: "Sample size and variance explained, from the maximum likelihood fit."

tibble(
  Participants = n_distinct(longitudinal$id),
  Observations = nrow(longitudinal),
  `R2 marginal` = sprintf("%.3f", as.numeric(lmm_r2$R2_marginal)),
  `R2 conditional` = sprintf("%.3f", as.numeric(lmm_r2$R2_conditional))
) |>
  kable()
```

Assumption-free companion.
Among participants who entered in August-September and were still measured in October-November, the within-person change between first and last measurement:

```{r}
#| label: paired-change

paired <- longitudinal |>
  filter(entry_cohort == "Aug-Sep 2025") |>
  group_by(id) |>
  filter(max(record_date) >= as_date("2025-10-01")) |>
  arrange(record_date, .by_group = TRUE) |>
  summarise(
    bmi_first = first(bmi),
    bmi_last = last(bmi),
    days_between = as.numeric(last(record_date) - first(record_date)),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(bmi_diff = bmi_last - bmi_first)

paired_change <- tidy(t.test(paired$bmi_diff)) |>
  transmute(
    n = nrow(paired),
    median_days_between = median(paired$days_between),
    mean_bmi_change = estimate,
    conf.low,
    conf.high,
    p.value
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: bayes-paired-change

# Intercept-only model on the within-person differences: the Bayesian
# counterpart of the one-sample t-test above
bayes_paired <- stan_glm(
  bmi_diff ~ 1,
  data = paired,
  chains = n_chains,
  iter = n_iter,
  seed = stan_seed,
  refresh = 0
)

bayes_paired_change <- as.numeric(as.matrix(bayes_paired, pars = "(Intercept)")) |>
  summarise_draws(c(`P(> 0)` = 0))
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-paired
#| tbl-cap: "Paired within-person BMI change, Aug-Sep entrants measured again in Oct-Nov, from both fits."

bind_rows(
  paired_change |>
    transmute(
      Fit = "One-sample t-test",
      `Change (95% interval)` = fmt_ci(
        mean_bmi_change,
        conf.low,
        conf.high,
        2
      ),
      Evidence = paste0("p = ", fmt_p(p.value))
    ),
  bayes_paired_change |>
    transmute(
      Fit = "Posterior (rstanarm)",
      `Change (95% interval)` = fmt_ci(median, conf.low, conf.high, 2),
      Evidence = paste0("P(> 0) = ", fmt_prob(`P(> 0)`))
    )
) |>
  mutate(
    N = nrow(paired),
    `Median days between` = median(paired$days_between),
    .before = 1
  ) |>
  kable()
```

This cannot be confounded by who joined when, so it carries the recovery claim.

```{r}
#| label: bayes-age-interaction

age_terms <- lmm_age$term

bayes_age <- map(age_terms, \(term) {
  slope_draws(bayes_bmi_time_age, term) |>
    summarise_draws(c(`P(> 0)` = 0)) |>
    mutate(term = term, .before = 1)
}) |>
  list_rbind()
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-lmm-age
#| tbl-cap: >-
#|   Effect modification of the BMI slope by age group, per 30 days, reference age under 30.
#|   The first row is the reference slope itself; the remaining rows are differences from it.
#|   P is the posterior probability that the term is greater than zero: a value near 0.5 means the data are uninformative about the direction, which is what the frequentist version could only express as a caveat.

bayes_age |>
  transmute(
    Term = if_else(
      term == "days_since_entry",
      "Slope, age under 30 (reference)",
      paste0("Difference in slope, ", str_remove(term, "days_since_entry:age"))
    ),
    `Posterior median (95% CrI)` = fmt_ci(median, conf.low, conf.high, 3),
    `P(> 0)` = fmt_prob(`P(> 0)`)
  ) |>
  kable()
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-lmm-age-compare
#| tbl-cap: "The same age terms from the maximum likelihood fit, for comparison."

lmm_age |>
  transmute(
    Term = if_else(
      term == "days_since_entry",
      "Slope, age under 30 (reference)",
      paste0("Difference in slope, ", str_remove(term, "days_since_entry:age"))
    ),
    `Estimate (95% CI)` = fmt_ci(
      estimate_per_30d,
      conf.low_per_30d,
      conf.high_per_30d,
      3
    ),
    `t` = sprintf("%.2f", statistic)
  ) |>
  kable()
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-trajectories
#| fig-cap: >-
#|   Individual BMI trajectories by calendar date among participants with two or more measurements.
#|   Each grey line is one participant; the orange line is the mixed model fit with its 95% confidence band.

longitudinal |>
  ggplot(aes(x = as.Date(record_date), y = bmi)) +
  geom_line(aes(group = id), alpha = 0.3, colour = "#01454f") +
```

### Sensitivity: generalised additive model

The dashboard figure uses a GAM with thin-plate smooths for date and pre-war BMI and a random effect for participant.
Refitted here for its fit statistics.
If the date smooth has effective degrees of freedom near 1, the linear slope in the mixed model is adequate.

```{r}
#| label: gam-sensitivity

gam_data <- longitudinal |>
  filter(!is.na(bmi_prewar)) |>
  mutate(day = as.integer(record_date), bmi_log = log(bmi))

gam_bmi_time <- gam(
  bmi_log ~ s(day, bs = "tp") + s(bmi_prewar, bs = "tp") + s(id, bs = "re"),
  data = gam_data,
  family = "gaussian"
)

gam_summary <- summary(gam_bmi_time)

gam_results <- tibble(
  term = rownames(gam_summary$s.table),
  edf = gam_summary$s.table[, "edf"],
  p.value = gam_summary$s.table[, "p-value"],
  n_observations = nrow(gam_data),
  deviance_explained = gam_summary$dev.expl,
  adj_r_squared = gam_summary$r.sq
)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-gam
#| tbl-cap: >-
#|   GAM smooth terms.
#|   An effective degrees of freedom of 1 for the date smooth means the relationship is linear over the observed window, so the mixed model slope above is adequate and is reported as the primary result.

gam_results |>
  transmute(
    Term = term,
    `Effective df` = sprintf("%.2f", edf),
    `p` = fmt_p(p.value)
  ) |>
  kable()
```

Deviance explained `r fmt_pct(100 * gam_results$deviance_explained[1])`, adjusted R-squared `r sprintf("%.3f", gam_results$adj_r_squared[1])`, on `r gam_results$n_observations[1]` observations.
Most of this is the participant random effect (effective df `r sprintf("%.0f", gam_results$edf[gam_results$term == "s(id)"])`), not the date smooth.

## Selection and measurement checks

Two participant groupings are compared against baseline characteristics.
Entry cohort asks whether the smaller weight loss among later joiners is recovery or a different sample.
Follow-up asks whether the participants with repeat measures represent the whole sample.

Both are equivalence claims: the argument being made is that the groups are similar enough that the comparison is not driven by composition.
A non-significant t-test cannot support that claim, because failing to reject a null is not evidence for it.
The t-tests are kept below for continuity with the draft, and each continuous comparison is additionally given an equivalence test against a region of practical equivalence.

```{r}
#| label: selection-checks

compare_categorical <- function(data, variable_name) {
  counts <- data |>
    filter(!is.na(.data[[variable_name]])) |>
    count(group_level = .group, level = .data[[variable_name]]) |>
    group_by(group_level) |>
    mutate(pct = 100 * n / sum(n)) |>
    ungroup()

  contingency_table <- table(data$.group, data[[variable_name]])

  counts |>
    mutate(
      variable = variable_name,
      variable_label = variable_labels[[variable_name]],
      p.value = suppressWarnings(chisq.test(contingency_table)$p.value)
    )
}

compare_continuous <- function(data, variable_name) {
  test <- t.test(reformulate(".group", variable_name), data = data)
  group_levels <- levels(factor(data$.group))

  tibble(
    variable = variable_name,
    variable_label = variable_labels[[variable_name]],
    level = "mean",
    group_level = group_levels,
    mean = as.numeric(test$estimate),
    # t.test reports level1 - level2; the table reports level2 - level1
    difference = test$estimate[[2]] - test$estimate[[1]],
    conf.low = -test$conf.int[2],
    conf.high = -test$conf.int[1],
    p.value = test$p.value
  )
}

compare_groups <- function(data, group_var, comparison_label) {
  data <- data |>
    mutate(.group = .data[[group_var]]) |>
    filter(!is.na(.group))
  stopifnot(length(levels(factor(data$.group))) == 2)

  bind_rows(
    map(
      c("age", "sex", "governorate_cat", "children", "role_cat"),
      \(variable_name) compare_categorical(data, variable_name)
    ) |>
      list_rbind(),
    map(
      c("bmi_prewar", "bmi_entry", "pct_weight_change", "age_years"),
      \(variable_name) compare_continuous(data, variable_name)
    ) |>
      list_rbind()
  ) |>
    mutate(comparison = comparison_label, .before = 1)
}

selection_checks <- bind_rows(
  compare_groups(baseline, "entry_cohort", "Entry cohort"),
  compare_groups(
    mutate(
      baseline,
      followup = factor(
        if_else(has_followup, "2+ observations", "Single observation"),
        levels = c("Single observation", "2+ observations")
      )
    ),
    "followup",
    "Follow-up"
  )
)

table_comparison_continuous <- function(comparison_label) {
  selection_checks |>
    filter(comparison == comparison_label, !is.na(difference)) |>
    mutate(value = sprintf("%.2f", mean)) |>
    select(
      Variable = variable_label,
      group_level,
      value,
      difference,
      conf.low,
      conf.high,
      p.value
    ) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = group_level, values_from = value) |>
    mutate(
      `Difference (95% CI)` = fmt_ci(difference, conf.low, conf.high, 2),
      `p` = fmt_p(p.value),
      .keep = "unused"
    ) |>
    kable()
}

table_comparison_categorical <- function(comparison_label) {
  selection_checks |>
    filter(comparison == comparison_label, is.na(difference)) |>
    mutate(cell = sprintf("%d (%.0f%%)", n, pct)) |>
    select(
      Characteristic = variable_label,
      Level = level,
      group_level,
      cell,
      p.value
    ) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = group_level, values_from = cell) |>
    mutate(`p` = fmt_p(p.value), .keep = "unused") |>
    kable()
}
```

```{r}
#| label: bayes-equivalence

# One two-group model per continuous characteristic, then an equivalence test
# of the group difference against a region of practical equivalence. The ROPE is
# bayestestR's default convention, +/- 0.1 standard deviations of the outcome,
# which is Kruschke's negligible-effect range; it is reported in the table so it
# can be judged rather than taken on trust.
equivalence_one <- function(data, group_var, variable_name, comparison_label) {
  model_data <- data |>
    mutate(.group = .data[[group_var]]) |>
    filter(!is.na(.group), !is.na(.data[[variable_name]]))

  fit <- stan_glm(
    reformulate(".group", variable_name),
    data = model_data,
    chains = n_chains,
    iter = n_iter,
    seed = stan_seed,
    refresh = 0
  )

  # The single non-intercept coefficient is the between-group difference
  group_term <- setdiff(names(coef(fit)), "(Intercept)")
  result <- equivalence_test(fit, parameters = group_term)

  tibble(
    comparison = comparison_label,
    variable = variable_name,
    variable_label = variable_labels[[variable_name]],
    rope_low = result$ROPE_low,
    rope_high = result$ROPE_high,
    pct_in_rope = result$ROPE_Percentage * 100,
    conf.low = result$CI_low,
    conf.high = result$CI_high,
    decision = result$ROPE_Equivalence
  )
}

continuous_characteristics <- c(
  "bmi_prewar",
  "bmi_entry",
  "pct_weight_change",
  "age_years"
)

baseline_followup <- baseline |>
  mutate(
    followup = factor(
      if_else(has_followup, "2+ observations", "Single observation"),
      levels = c("Single observation", "2+ observations")
    )
  )

equivalence_checks <- bind_rows(
  map(
    continuous_characteristics,
    \(variable_name) {
      equivalence_one(baseline, "entry_cohort", variable_name, "Entry cohort")
    }
  ) |>
    list_rbind(),
  map(
    continuous_characteristics,
    \(variable_name) {
      equivalence_one(
        baseline_followup,
        "followup",
        variable_name,
        "Follow-up"
      )
    }
  ) |>
    list_rbind()
)

table_equivalence <- function(comparison_label) {
  equivalence_checks |>
    filter(comparison == comparison_label) |>
    transmute(
      Characteristic = variable_label,
      `Difference, 95% CrI` = sprintf("%.2f to %.2f", conf.low, conf.high),
      ROPE = sprintf("%.2f to %.2f", rope_low, rope_high),
      `% of posterior in ROPE` = fmt_pct(pct_in_rope),
      Verdict = decision
    ) |>
    kable()
}
```

### Entry cohort comparison

```{r}
#| label: tbl-cohort-continuous
#| tbl-cap: >-
#|   Continuous baseline characteristics by entry cohort.
#|   Difference is Oct-Nov minus Aug-Sep.

table_comparison_continuous("Entry cohort")
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-cohort-equivalence
#| tbl-cap: >-
#|   Equivalence test of the same characteristics by entry cohort.
#|   ROPE is the region of practical equivalence, +/- 0.1 standard deviations of the characteristic.
#|   "Accepted" means the whole 95% credible interval falls inside that region, so the groups can be treated as equivalent; "Rejected" means it falls entirely outside; "Undecided" means the data cannot distinguish the two.

table_equivalence("Entry cohort")
```

The two cohorts had effectively identical pre-war BMI but differed at entry, which points to a period effect rather than to the later wave being a systematically lighter or heavier sample.
The equivalence test is what licenses the first half of that sentence: pre-war BMI is not merely non-significant, it is inside the region of practical equivalence.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-cohort-categorical
#| tbl-cap: "Categorical baseline characteristics by entry cohort."

table_comparison_categorical("Entry cohort")
```

### Follow-up comparison

```{r}
#| label: tbl-followup-continuous
#| tbl-cap: >-
#|   Continuous baseline characteristics by whether a participant contributed repeat measurements.
#|   Difference is 2+ observations minus single observation.

table_comparison_continuous("Follow-up")
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-followup-equivalence
#| tbl-cap: >-
#|   Equivalence test of the same characteristics by whether a participant contributed repeat measurements.
#|   This is the test that matters for generalising the follow-up results to the full sample.

table_equivalence("Follow-up")
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-followup-categorical
#| tbl-cap: "Categorical baseline characteristics by whether a participant contributed repeat measurements."

table_comparison_categorical("Follow-up")
```

### Digit preference in recalled pre-war weight

Recalled pre-war weight against measured weight at entry.
Both are heaped on whole kilograms, so the measured value is not a clean reference: scales and recorders round too.
The excess heaping in the recalled value over the measured one is what quantifies how much coarser recall was.

```{r}
#| label: digit-preference

is_whole_kg <- function(weight) abs(weight - round(weight)) < 1e-8

digit_preference <- cross_sectional |>
  select(id, Recalled = weight_prewar, Measured = weight_entry) |>
  pivot_longer(
    c(Recalled, Measured),
    names_to = "source",
    values_to = "weight"
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(weight)) |>
  group_by(source) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    pct_whole_kg = 100 * mean(is_whole_kg(weight)),
    pct_ends_0_or_5_kg = 100 *
      mean(is_whole_kg(weight) & round(weight) %% 5 == 0),
    pct_ends_0_kg = 100 *
      mean(is_whole_kg(weight) & round(weight) %% 10 == 0),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-digits
#| tbl-cap: "Rounding in recalled pre-war weight compared with measured weight at entry."

digit_preference |>
  transmute(
    Source = source,
    N = n,
    `Whole kg` = fmt_pct(pct_whole_kg),
    `Ends in 0 or 5 kg` = fmt_pct(pct_ends_0_or_5_kg),
    `Ends in 0 kg` = fmt_pct(pct_ends_0_kg)
  ) |>
  kable()
```

### Comparison with the 2020 representative survey

```{r}
#| label: external-comparison

# The aggregated file carries means only, so SDs for the published column must
# come from the paper: flagged rather than fabricated.
survey_2020 <- read_csv(
  here("data", "raw", "gaza_survey2020_kcal_bmi_agg.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
) |>
  transmute(
    age_band = age_cat,
    sex = if_else(gender == "f", "Female", "Male"),
    bmi_2020 = weight / height^2,
    sd_bmi_2020 = NA_real_
  )

external_comparison <- cross_sectional |>
  filter(!is.na(age_years), age_years >= 40, !is.na(bmi_prewar)) |>
  mutate(
    age_band = cut(
      age_years,
      breaks = c(40, 50, 60, 70, 120),
      right = FALSE,
      labels = c("[40,50)", "[50,60)", "[60,70)", "[70,120]")
    )
  ) |>
  group_by(age_band, sex) |>
  summarise(
    n_this_study = n(),
    mean_bmi_prewar = mean(bmi_prewar),
    sd_bmi_prewar = sd(bmi_prewar),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(age_band = as.character(age_band), sex = as.character(sex)) |>
  left_join(survey_2020, by = c("age_band", "sex"))
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-external
#| tbl-cap: "Pre-war BMI in this study compared with the 2020 cross-sectional survey (Hamad et al.), by age band and sex."

external_comparison |>
  transmute(
    `Age band` = age_band,
    Sex = sex,
    `This study, n` = n_this_study,
    `This study, mean BMI (SD)` = sprintf(
      "%.1f (%.1f)",
      mean_bmi_prewar,
      sd_bmi_prewar
    ),
    `2020 survey, mean BMI` = sprintf("%.1f", bmi_2020),
    `2020 survey, SD` = if_else(
      is.na(sd_bmi_2020),
      "not in aggregated file",
      sprintf("%.1f", sd_bmi_2020)
    )
  ) |>
  kable()
```

The aggregated 2020 file carries means only.
SDs for the published column have to come from the paper or from whoever holds the microdata.
